videos.headline: Broad to Rahul, out Caught by Buttler!! Stuart Broad has his first wicket of the game in his homeground. Skipper Root reaction says it all... England were desperate for a wicket and there were spraying it all over conceding one too many boundaries in the last few overs. This should offer some relief. Just the ideal length from Broad, keeps it in the fifth stump corridor and gets the ball to nip away ever so slightly drawing a healthy edge through to the keeper. Rahul was on the shuffle and got too close to the line to avoid any temptation. Hung his bat out to dry and sent a thick outside edge. Rahul c Buttler b Broad 26(38) [4s-6]

Bumrah to Root, out Caught by Pant!! The new ball has done the trick for India - Root falls after a sublime hundred and he's absolutely livid with himself, not Kohli though as he celebrates with vigour. On a good length and in that channel just outside off, Root didn't need to play at that, perhaps he was playing for the angle. This straightened on him, some extra lift as well, good enough to find the edge and Pant does the rest. But Root falls after a splendid hundred, has has set this game up nicely, one way or the other. Root c Pant b Bumrah 109(172) [4s-14]

Thakur to Buttler, out Bowled!! Oh dear! That's a horrible misjudgement from Buttler and India get the start they needed after the break - the in-ducker, pitched outside off and kept coming back into the right-hander, Buttler thought he had covered for the movement, trusted the bounce on this pitch as he shouldered arms. Bad mistake - the ball did enough to clatter into top of the off-stump and Shardul is off on his celebration run. A shake of the head from Buttler he walks off. England are effectively 142 for 6 now. Buttler b Thakur 17(22) [4s-3]

Thakur to Lawrence, out Lbw!! And it doesn't take Thakur long to correct his line. And correct he does! Dead straight stuff this: on a length, on middle, with Lawrence playing outside the line entirely for some reason. It's not that it swung back in either. Anyway, he's trapped plumb on the front knee roll in front of middle, and then he burns a review as well. Three reds, dark reds. Lawrence lbw b Thakur 25(32) [4s-4]

Siraj to Bairstow, out Caught by Jadeja!! It's a proper innocuous drag down. And Bairstow's nailed his pull, swivelling, swinging hard, flat. But well, well, he's found a way to pick out the man at deep square leg to perfection. Siraj has his finger on his lips in the staring send-off. It's a massive moment, and quite like his first innings dismissal after looking so good, could be the twist in this innings. Bairstow c Jadeja b Siraj 30(50) [4s-4]

Bumrah to Sibley, out Caught by Pant!! It goes gloomy upwards and it goes gloomy downwards for England. All in a matter of moments. Sibley has thrown it away after doing all the hardwork of surviving some scathing spells. Was well wide of off-stump and could have left it alone, but such are Sibley's compulsive instincts while shuffling across that he tends to go pushy-pokey on the move and there's a major chunk of inside edge that flew to the left of Pant to complete a splendid diving catch. Sibley c Pant b Bumrah 28(133) [4s-2]

Bumrah to Crawley, out Caught by Pant!! If Burns' poke was compulsive, Crawley's is clearly unnecessary. It's a fifth-stump line, but Crawley, with his typically uncertain early shuffle, has gotten himself too close to it, and this is forced to play at it in front of his body. Anyway, Bumrah's gotten this to zip away off the deck, square him up, draw the flat-footed outside-edge, for Pant to dive low to his right. Crawley c Pant b Bumrah 6(7) [4s-1]

Siraj to Rory Burns, out Caught by Pant!! There comes the compulsive poke, and there comes the nick. Burns, with his extensive overbalance on his leg-side, doesn't really move his feet,and Siraj, with this perfect scrambled-seam angler across in the channel, gets is close enough this time. Thus the tentative prod, and thus the outside-edge to the keeper. Rory Burns c Pant b Siraj 18(49) [4s-3]

Robinson to Bumrah, out Caught by Broad!! That'll end the fun. And Robinson, coming back after all his Twitter troubles, and sneaking under the radar all innings with Jimmy bagging the headlines, has pipped him to the fifer. It's his bouncer he's gone back to here, something Bumrah's swung hard to, top-edged, with Broad doing a fine job at fine leg to swirl under this, tumble, and importantly, gather cleanly. Bumrah c Broad b Robinson 28(34) [4s-3 6s-1]

Robinson to Shami, out Bowled!! Flat-footed waft, and boom. Robinson keeps it simple: full, straight, on the stumps, with the ball sneaking through Shami's drive, and deflecting off his back pad onto middle-stump. Shami b Robinson 13(20)

Robinson to Jadeja, out Caught by Broad!! A steepler and Jadeja falls in the attempt to get some quick runs - hit the deck stuff from Robinson, on a glo and angling across the left-hander, Jadeja was never going to get behind the line, threw his bat on the big drive, the bat turned on imapct and he sliced it high and towards mid-off. Broad ran back, kept his eyes on the ball and held on. Jadeja was going on so well, was this shot needed? He falls after a fine effort though. Jadeja c Broad b Robinson 56(86) [4s-8 6s-1]

Anderson to Thakur, out Caught by Root!! Edged and caught! No Gabba heroics fom Shardul and Anderson is all smiles now. Lovely little delivery and a neat catch from Root, sliding to his left. On a good length and in that channel just outside off, once again straightening with the seam and drawing the batsman into a hard-handed push, finds the edge and Root goes with soft hands, clasps it neatly and England have struck twice after lunch. Fourth wicket for Anderson and he's on a roll. Thakur c Root b Anderson 0(6)

Anderson to Rahul, out Caught by Buttler!! There's wicket number 620 for Anderson - he's distraught with himself as he walks away, Rahul, will feel he missed out on a hundred. Anderson gets past Kumble with that wicket. Pitched up and the ball straightened with the angle, drew Rahul into the drive, he's played that shot very well right through, but this time he manages only a thin edge through to the keeper. Didn't do anything wrong, but that's the wicket England wanted. India's lead is 22, but they're into the lower order now. Rahul c Buttler b Anderson 84(214) [4s-12]

Robinson to Pant, out Caught by Bairstow!! Easy as you like. Looked like a trap from England and Bairstow barely moved to accept this dolly at cover. Hits the ball on a good length and gets it to stop on the batsman with a hint of exra bounce, Pant was on the front foot and he was through his shot (check-drive) a fraction too early inducing it off the splice of the bat and into the lap of YJB on the off-side. Pant c Bairstow b Robinson 25(20) [4s-3 6s-1]

Robinson to Rahul, out Rahane Run Out!! Another direct hit and Rahane is run-out. Oh dear! This is suicidal running from Rahane, there was absolutely no run there and Kohli shakes his head in the dressing room. India are crumbling after the break - not sure where Rahane was heading to after Rahul dropped one in front of cover-point - he did take a step forward but yelled his partner to go back, but Rahane was backing up a long way, has to turn around and he was always struggling. Bairstow rushed in from backward point, takes aim and breaks the stumps, with the Indian vice-captain well short. Rahane run out (Bairstow) 5(5)
Anderson to Rahane, no run, that's an anti-climax - tried the big inswinger and spilled it down leg, Rahane was looking to flick and missed

Anderson to Pujara, out Caught by Buttler!! A corker and England are celebrating. Has the ball carried through to the keeper? The soft signal is OUT, there's a definite edge and the ball has carried through to Buttler cleanly. Pujara is OUT. His misery in English conditions continue - but this was a superb delivery from the wily seamer. Pitched up in that channel around off, the anglekept coming back, drew Pujara forward and then wickedly swung away late, catching Pujara's edge on the forward push, nicely carries through to Buttler, who slid across to his right. Suddenly, India have lost two after a strong start. Pujara c Buttler b Anderson 4(16)

Robinson to Rohit, out Caught by Sam Curran!! A bouncer, and Rohit with a compulsive pull holing out at fine leg. It's the Australia story all over again. There's nothing called being set with him. And Robinson, perhaps with the first short one all morning, has sucked him in. So it was short, perhaps even over head high as Sharma went to hook, with the ball getting big on him, drawing an uncontrolled top-edge, right to a waiting Curran by the boundary. Rohit c Sam Curran b Robinson 36(107) [4s-6]

Bumrah to Anderson, out Bowled!! Right, Bumrah doesn't need the umpire's help - another searing inswinging yorker and it's too good for the England number 11. Came from round the wicket and speared one into the left-hander, Anderson is way too late in getting the bat down and hears the death-rattle, the base of off-stump is rattled and England have been bundled out for 183. Anderson b Bumrah 1(11)

Bumrah to Broad, out Lbw!! The word plumb would give itself plumb out lbw for this. It was that easy. Bumrah almost stopped appealing for he knew there was only going to be one decision. Full and curling in from leg-stump towards off, there's Broad's pad in between all of that, looking to play off the back foot and misses. Bingo! Broad lbw b Bumrah 4(3) [4s-1]

Thakur to Robinson, out Caught by Shami!! That is catching practice for Shami. Shardul Thakur couldn't have asked for an easier Test wicket. You earn them with hardwork, they say, but when luck decides to combine you become unstoppable. A poor shot from the highly-rated Ollie Robinson. A tame chip straight into the lap of mid-on. Shardul Thakur has turned the game on its head in a matter of 4 deliveries... Robinson c Shami b Thakur 0(3)

Thakur to Root, out Lbw!! All those hundred kilometers to Mumbai train journey on a daily basis is now worth it! Shardul Thakur perhaps has had the biggest wicket of his career so far, and might well be the biggest of this game and the series. "I can give it out from up here," Bumble on air soon as he saw the ball hitting the pad. It was dead and Root had no way back. The cunning nip-backer from Shardul Thakur that came in from a really full length, leaving no chance for the England skipper to survive. He was a fraction late on the flick and by the time he couple spot the ball, the umpire's finger was up a flash. Huge wicket for India. Root lbw b Thakur 64(108) [4s-11]

Bumrah to Buttler, out Caught by Pant!! This was always coming. Jos Buttler getting out for nought may not create enough headlines, but the manner in which he played will come under scrutiny. A very disappointing effort from the senior pro. Kept poking at deliveries outside off and to make matters worse, he was playing with hard hands which goes onto accentuate the risk of white-ball instincts. The one that eventually consumed him. Having played 17 dots, Buttler was desperately looking for a release shot but the delivery from Bumrah was anything but that. It came in from wide of the crease and straightened enough to graze the outside edge on the forward push. The footwork was all over the place and looked really ugly. Buttler c Pant b Bumrah 0(18)

Shami to Lawrence, out Caught by Pant!! Burns, Sibley and now Lawrence follows suit. Mohammed Shami has three. How badly did he needed this luck? Was one of India's best bowlers last time they toured England, but luck wasn't on his side. Today he is unleashing some pearlers and this one is just the kind of luck you need as a bowler. Swinging into the pads from a length and makes Lawrence think it was a boundary-hitting opportunity, chases with a closed bat face and sends a fine tickle to the left of the keeper. Huge appeal and umpire Richard Kettleborough had his finger up in a flash. Lawrence looks guilty and off he walks... Lawrence c Pant b Shami 0(4)

Shami to Bairstow, out Lbw!! India review: It's a sharp in-cutter, jagging in off a length and trapping Bairstow in his crease after comfortably going past his inside-edge. Once again, there were two noises and this time Shardul Thakur - at mid-on - is whom Kohli has trusted with his judgement to take it upstairs. He's convinced there's no bat. And no bat it is. The two noises is ball hitting either pad, and HawkEye is plumb with three reds. Bairstow lbw b Shami 29(71) [4s-4]

Shami to Sibley, out Caught by Rahul!! Oh dear! There was a fielder at short mid-wicket and Sibley has fallen right into the trap. It's KL Rahul and he couldn't have hoped for an easier catch. Pitched up and shaping back into the right-hander, Sibley fell across on the flick, closed the bat face a fraction too early, off the leading edge and it's a dolly to KL. India have started brightly after lunch, a crestfallen Sibley walks off - was looking to go square, but didn't control his shot. Sibley c Rahul b Shami 18(70) [4s-2]

Siraj to Crawley, out Caught by Pant!! Mohammed Siraj into the wickets column. Bowls one that's similar to the third and this time there's a clear inside edge that carries through to the left of the keeper. Crawley was once again caught late in reacting to the nip-backer and by the time he got his bat down, it was still angling and poking forward. Thick inside edge onto pad and through to the keeper. Kohli was very circumspect about the review and Pant was the one who convinced him to challenge the onfield call. Crawley c Pant b Siraj 27(68) [4s-4]

Bumrah to Rory Burns, out Lbw!! Typically Burns -- late with his feet, falling across in his overbalancing stance, and then getting done in by a sharp inswinger. And typically Bumrah -- setting him up with three outswingers, only to sneak in a quick one coming in, beating the inside-edge comfortably to pin him in front of middle. Now, there were two noises, and given how long Burns' taken to review this, it's surely not the bat. Yep, front pad and back pad. And an umpire's call as it clips the top of middle. Top, dream start. Rory Burns lbw b Bumrah 0(5)
